site.name: migration-atlas
site.summary: Migration Atlas — animal migration tracking (local demo) Fictional global animal-tracking atlas. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Atlas Three columns: left filter rail, center map + player, right inspector. The map is a hand-rolled SVG world (equirectangular projection) drawn from inline continent polygons and lon/lat graticules. Seven species are pre-loaded, each with a per-individual synthetic track of 12 monthly waypoints. Filters (left): species toggles with sample size counts, study year, display toggles (trail line, monthly position dots, stop-over polygons). Player (below map): slider scrubs through January → December. Play / pause button animates the season; speed selector controls cadence. As the slider advances, individuals' trails extend.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full migration-atlas system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Migration Atlas provides robust, real-time filtering and dynamic SVG visualization of animal tracking data across viewports. However, the experience is hampered by missing visual feedback on key functional buttons and dead navigation links. On mobile, usability is notably degraded by undersized touch targets for filters and cramped, overlapping typography on the timeline axis.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full migration-atlas system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start by verifying global header actions and navigation links. It will then methodically exercise the left-hand filter panel, testing species selection, search, and display toggles. Next, the focus will shift to the center map's playback controls and timeline slider, followed by interacting with the map itself to trigger the right-hand inspector. Finally, a mobile viewport check will assess layout degradation and tap target sizes.
assumptions: Nav links like 'Studies' and 'Methods' may just be hash links as this is a local demo, but their states should still be checked.
Map interactions (clicking trails/dots) rely on SVG elements which might require precise clicking.
The right panel 'Individual' section updates dynamically when map elements are clicked.
The player animation updates the visual state of the SVG map and the 'Current Month' text.
risk_hotspots: SVG map element clickability (trails and pins)
Timeline slider scrubbing and playback animation synchronization
Small tap targets for checkboxes and header links on mobile devices

phases.title: Header and Global Actions
phases.objective: Verify the functionality of top navigation links and utility buttons.
key_checks: Click 'Cite this view' and 'Save view' to observe system response (modals, alerts, or no-ops)
Click top nav links ('Studies', 'Methods', etc.) to check for page routing or dead links
exit_criteria: All header links and buttons have been interacted with and their outcomes noted.

phases.title: Data Filtering and Display Settings
phases.objective: Test the left-hand rail filters to ensure they update the map and aggregate stats.
key_checks: Type in 'Filter species…' input and verify if checkbox list filters
Toggle various species checkboxes and verify 'SPECIES SHOWN' and 'INDIVIDUALS' counts update
Change 'STUDY YEAR' dropdown and observe changes
Toggle 'Show trail', 'Show monthly positions', and 'Show stop-over polygons'
exit_criteria: Filter controls are proven to manipulate the data visualization state and summary metrics.

phases.title: Playback Controls
phases.objective: Validate the animation and timeline scrubbing functionality.
key_checks: Click Play (▶) button and observe the month slider advancing and map trails extending
Change playback speed via the dropdown and verify cadence
Manually scrub the month slider and verify the 'CURRENT MONTH' text and map trails update accordingly
exit_criteria: Player controls successfully manipulate the temporal state of the map data.

phases.title: Map Interactivity and Inspection
phases.objective: Ensure individual tracks can be inspected via map interaction.
key_checks: Click on a visible track or pin within the SVG map
Verify the right-hand 'Individual' inspector panel populates with specific animal data
exit_criteria: At least one individual track has been successfully inspected and detailed in the right panel.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Check
phases.objective: Evaluate the complex 3-column layout and small tap targets on a mobile screen.
key_checks: Verify layout stacking (do filters, map, and inspector stack logically?)
Interact with species checkboxes and playback controls to check for tap target difficulties
exit_criteria: Mobile layout is fully reviewed and any blocking usability issues are logged.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all left-panel filters, bottom playback controls, top header actions, and map inspection clicks.
coverage_targets.mobile: Ensure the 3-column desktop layout gracefully degrades and controls remain usable on mobile.

notes: Since the map uses custom SVG rendering, standard DOM click coordinates might be tricky. Aim for clearly visible trails or dots.

findings.user_goal: Save or cite the current map view
findings.problem: Clicking the 'Cite this view' and 'Save view' buttons provides no visible feedback, such as a modal, toast notification, or clipboard confirmation.
findings.evidence: Repeatedly noted in session memory: 'The 'Cite this view' button produces no visible feedback... leaving users uncertain if the action succeeded.'
findings.why_it_matters: Without immediate system feedback, users do not know if their action was successfully registered, which erodes trust and can lead to repeated, frustrated clicks.
findings.suggestion: Implement a brief toast notification (e.g., 'View saved!' or 'Citation copied') or open a modal dialogue when these global action buttons are triggered.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to other sections like 'Submit a track' or 'Studies'
findings.problem: Primary navigation links ('Studies', 'Submit a track', 'Methods', 'About') are dead links (href='#') that append a hash to the URL without triggering any page change or modal.
findings.evidence: Session memory details multiple tests where clicking these top navigation links resulted in no visible routing, scrolling, or feedback.
findings.why_it_matters: Users looking for more context or aiming to contribute data hit immediate dead ends, creating a broken experience that makes the site feel incomplete.
findings.suggestion: If these are stubbed for a demo, provide a 'Coming soon' tooltip or modal. Otherwise, ensure they route correctly to their respective pages or sections.

findings.user_goal: Change the timeframe of the displayed data
findings.problem: Selecting a new year in the 'STUDY YEAR' dropdown (e.g., '2024 season') updates the dropdown value, but the main dashboard heading remains stuck on 'Migration Atlas — 2025 season'.
findings.evidence: Observation in steps-31-36: 'Selecting '2024 season'... fails to update the dashboard heading below... remaining stuck on 'Migration Atlas — 2025 season'.'
findings.why_it_matters: Desynchronized text creates conflicting information, leaving users confused about which year's data they are actually viewing.
findings.suggestion: Bind the dashboard title text to the current state of the 'Study Year' select input so they update synchronously.

findings.user_goal: Toggle species and display filters on a mobile device
findings.problem: The checkboxes for species and display filters have a tap target of only 13x13px, which falls drastically below mobile touch target guidelines.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings highlight 13x13px tap targets for 'Humpback whale', 'Show trail', 'Show monthly positions', and 'Show stop-over polygons'.
findings.why_it_matters: Extremely small tap targets cause usability friction, forcing mobile users to tap very precisely to avoid accidental selections or missed taps.
findings.suggestion: Increase the touch target area to at least 44x44px by adding padding to the `<label>` elements and ensuring the entire label row is clickable.

findings.user_goal: Track the current month on the animation timeline
findings.problem: The month labels below the timeline slider lack adequate horizontal spacing on mobile, causing the text to run together into an unreadable string ('JanFebMarAprMayJun...').
findings.evidence: Visible in the mobile screenshot (agentic-49-click-mobile.png) and noted in step 37-42 observations.
findings.why_it_matters: Overlapping text creates visual clutter and makes it difficult for users to map the slider thumb to the correct month.
findings.suggestion: Adjust the flex/grid spacing for the month labels on smaller screens, or consider showing only every other month (or just quarters) to ensure adequate typographic breathing room.

findings.user_goal: Interact with form controls using assistive technology
findings.problem: Several form controls—including the 'Study Year' select, the timeline range slider, and the playback speed select—lack explicit programmatic labels or 'aria-label' attributes.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings repeatedly flag 'Missing input label' for ux-11 (Study Year select), ux-16 (timeline slider), and ux-17 (speed select).
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users rely on programmatic labels to understand the purpose of form elements. Without them, the interface becomes difficult or impossible to navigate via assistive tech.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit `<label>` elements linked via 'id' and 'for' attributes, or use 'aria-label' attributes to describe the purpose of these inputs.
